evidence.section: Wagner–Fischer 1974: The String-to-String Correction Problem, Dynamic Programming, and Edit Distance
evidence.excerpt: Wagner and Fischer do not begin by writing down a three-way recurrence and declaring it obvious. They first define a general weighted theory of edit operations, reduce arbitrary edit sequences to order-preserving structures they call traces , prove that minimum edit-sequence cost equals minimum trace cost, derive the dynamic-programming recurrence from the structure of an optimal trace, give an explicit algorithm for computing the distance, give a second algorithm for recovering a minimum-cost trace, prove the traceback algorithm correct, and finally show how the same framework computes a longest common subsequence.
